findings.summary: Live acquisition provenance previously admitted an arbitrary endpoint or injected transport.
findings.failure_scenario: Untrusted catalog content is mislabeled as live OpenRouter data.
findings.impact: Misleading provenance could influence candidate selection.
findings.minimum_fix: Fix the live endpoint and separate captured-response acquisition.

findings.summary: One malformed entry previously could abort the entire untrusted catalog.
findings.failure_scenario: One invalid provider, identifier, or decimal denies a refresh containing other valid entries.
findings.impact: Untrusted metadata could cause catalog-wide denial of service.
findings.minimum_fix: Validate and exclude each entry independently.

findings.summary: The initial candidate retroactively expanded its own planning scope.
findings.failure_scenario: An implementation makes an out-of-scope edit legal by editing its own packet source.
findings.impact: The reviewed task boundary becomes ineffective.
findings.minimum_fix: Authorize the exact test paths in a separate process task merged before recompilation.

findings.summary: The provider catalog byte cap was previously applied only after full response buffering.
findings.failure_scenario: A chunked or inaccurately sized response exhausts memory before validation.
findings.impact: Untrusted provider data can deny service to the CLI process.
findings.minimum_fix: Count decoded stream bytes and cancel immediately above the cap.

findings.summary: The shortlist previously admitted models unable to fit representative usage.
findings.failure_scenario: A cheap undersized model displaces an evaluable model in the bounded shortlist.
findings.impact: Candidate budget is wasted and recommendation evidence cannot be valid.
findings.minimum_fix: Filter context windows against prompt plus completion tokens before ranking.

findings.summary: Projected workload cost previously omitted the per-million divisor.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid shortlist reports projected dollar cost one million times too high.
findings.impact: Savings reports and downstream financial decisions are materially wrong.
findings.minimum_fix: Divide the exact weighted per-million price by one million before reporting.

findings.summary: Captured catalog files previously bypassed bounded ingestion before response construction.
findings.failure_scenario: A hostile repository capture is fully allocated before the catalog byte cap runs.
findings.impact: Untrusted repository input can deny service to the CLI process.
findings.minimum_fix: Stream the file through the same bounded reader used for provider responses.

findings.summary: Live refreshes previously accepted caller-controlled freshness timestamps.
findings.failure_scenario: A live fetch is recorded with a caller-selected future observation time.
findings.impact: Stale model metadata can masquerade as current evidence.
findings.minimum_fix: Derive live freshness from the acquisition clock and reserve explicit timestamps for captures.

findings.summary: Same-digest snapshot reuse previously trusted metadata outside the content digest.
findings.failure_scenario: A preseeded snapshot reuses valid models with forged source, identity, or future provenance.
findings.impact: A successful observation can bind attacker-controlled catalog provenance.
findings.minimum_fix: Require canonical OpenRouter identity and temporally compatible provenance before reuse.

findings.summary: Repository snapshot replay previously buffered unbounded files before parsing.
findings.failure_scenario: An oversized checked-in snapshot exhausts the CLI heap before schema validation.
findings.impact: Untrusted repository input can deny service during offline replay.
findings.minimum_fix: Apply one streaming byte limit to every repository JSON and scanned source read.

findings.summary: Offline shortlist replay previously accepted noncanonical snapshot identity.
findings.failure_scenario: A valid model digest is replayed under an arbitrary source or unrelated snapshot ID.
findings.impact: Candidate evidence can cite misleading or reusable catalog identity.
findings.minimum_fix: Require the OpenRouter source and digest-derived snapshot ID at storage and replay boundaries.

findings.summary: Conflicting duplicate provider model IDs previously aborted the entire refresh.
findings.failure_scenario: Two valid but conflicting rows with one ID make every valid catalog entry unavailable.
findings.impact: Ambiguous untrusted metadata can deny catalog refresh service.
findings.minimum_fix: Collapse identical rows and exclude conflicting IDs before snapshot construction.

findings.summary: A valid catalog row previously remained eligible when another row with the same ID failed normalization.
findings.failure_scenario: A complete row is paired with an invalid duplicate whose pricing, context, or capabilities cannot be trusted.
findings.impact: Ambiguous provider metadata can remain eligible for execution despite fail-closed policy.
findings.minimum_fix: Count raw model IDs before normalization and exclude the entire repeated ID unless every row normalizes identically.

findings.summary: Repository catalog captures previously defaulted missing acquisition time to import time.
findings.failure_scenario: A stale checked-in provider response is imported without --observed-at and appears freshly acquired.
findings.impact: Stale pricing and capabilities can support a shortlist under forged freshness.
findings.minimum_fix: Require an explicit offset-aware acquisition timestamp for every captured response.

findings.summary: A failed observation write previously could leave a directly replayable orphan snapshot.
findings.failure_scenario: A duplicate refresh ID or filesystem failure interrupts persistence after snapshot publication.
findings.impact: Repository state can contain catalog evidence without the acquisition record required to establish provenance.
findings.minimum_fix: Commit the observation before publishing a new snapshot and roll it back if snapshot publication fails.

findings.summary: Captured responses previously accepted timestamps arbitrarily far ahead of the trusted clock.
findings.failure_scenario: A future-dated capture persists a snapshot that blocks legitimate same-content live refreshes as temporally incompatible.
findings.impact: Untrusted repository metadata can poison freshness evidence and prevent current observations.
findings.minimum_fix: Reject captured timestamps more than a bounded clock-skew allowance ahead of the trusted process clock.

findings.summary: File-backed catalog writes previously followed symlinked store directories.
findings.failure_scenario: An untrusted checkout points snapshots or observations at a directory outside the configured store.
findings.impact: Catalog refresh can create attacker-directed files outside its intended repository location.
findings.minimum_fix: Reject symbolic-link path components and verify resolved write parents remain beneath the resolved store root.

findings.summary: Tool-choice-only metadata previously advertised full tool-call capability.
findings.failure_scenario: An untrusted row exposes tool_choice without accepting the tools definitions required by the call site.
findings.impact: An incompatible model can consume bounded candidate budget and fail during execution.
findings.minimum_fix: Require explicit tools parameter support before setting tool-call capability.

findings.summary: Catalog refresh previously had no deadline for response headers or body consumption.
findings.failure_scenario: The provider accepts a connection but never completes headers or its response stream.
findings.impact: The CLI can hang indefinitely without recording required refresh-failure evidence.
findings.minimum_fix: Apply one bounded abort deadline across acquisition and body consumption and persist timeout failure evidence.

findings.summary: Immutable catalog snapshots previously wrote directly to their final digest path.
findings.failure_scenario: Disk exhaustion or process interruption leaves a truncated digest-named snapshot that blocks a later refresh.
findings.impact: Incomplete evidence can occupy an immutable identity and cause durable refresh failure or data loss.
findings.minimum_fix: Write a complete same-directory temporary file, atomically link it into the digest path without overwrite, and remove the temporary file.

findings.summary: Concurrent refreshes previously decided snapshot reuse before atomic publication.
findings.failure_scenario: Two refreshes for one unseen digest both record reusedSnapshot false even though one loses the publication race and reuses the winner.
findings.impact: Immutable refresh evidence can misstate the storage action that actually occurred.
findings.minimum_fix: Serialize snapshot inspection, observation publication, and snapshot publication per content digest.

findings.summary: Immutable refresh observations previously wrote directly to their final ID path.
findings.failure_scenario: Disk exhaustion or process interruption leaves a truncated observation that blocks retry with the same refresh ID.
findings.impact: Incomplete evidence can occupy an immutable identity and require manual recovery.
findings.minimum_fix: Write a complete same-directory temporary file and atomically link it into the observation path without overwrite.

findings.summary: Successful observations previously became visible before a newly referenced snapshot.
findings.failure_scenario: A concurrent reader or process termination observes successful refresh evidence before its exact snapshot exists.
findings.impact: Repository evidence can claim a successful refresh that is not replayable.
findings.minimum_fix: Publish the snapshot first and use the atomic successful observation as the final commit record, rolling back on ordinary failure.

findings.summary: Offline replay previously trusted unauthenticated snapshot freshness metadata.
findings.failure_scenario: A checked-in snapshot retains its digest and ID while observedAt is edited to a future time.
findings.impact: Candidate evidence can cite forged catalog freshness.
findings.minimum_fix: Require matching successful refresh evidence, reject temporally incompatible observations, and bind its ID and time into the shortlist.

findings.summary: Rejected provider responses previously left their response body active.
findings.failure_scenario: An HTTP error or oversized declared response retains an unbounded body after the refresh deadline is cleared.
findings.impact: Repeated failures can retain network resources or delay CLI termination.
findings.minimum_fix: Cancel rejected response bodies before recording failure evidence.

residual_risks: Live OpenRouter transport remains outside offline CI.
Windows-specific filesystem behavior is outside the current V1 matrix.

state_impact: Refreshes create bounded immutable observations and snapshots.
source_of_truth_changes: Repository snapshots and their digests are authoritative for replay.
feedback_plan: Remote CI and latest-head Codex review replay the final branch.
blast_radius: Scanner, evaluator, recommendation, and patch behavior remain unchanged.
rollback_or_deletion_test: Deleting the package and CLI commands restores the prior workspace without manifest migration.
systems_questions.system_model_summary: All untrusted repository and provider inputs are byte- and time-bounded and rejected response bodies are canceled; captures require explicit acquisition time within bounded future skew; catalog rows normalize per ID and advertise only explicit capabilities; immutable snapshots and observations publish atomically without overwrite, with the snapshot first and its successful observation as the commit record; per-digest serialization binds reuse evidence to the actual storage decision; file stores reject symlink redirection; replay requires canonical digest-derived identity plus matching successful freshness evidence and binds both into the shortlist; live freshness is clock-derived; and hard filters precede exact-cost ranking.
